Content:
Suppose that we have the two polynomials [MATH: 6x^2 + x +1] and [MATH: 2x^2 - 3x + 6], and we want to add them. To do that, we put a plus sign between the two, collect like terms, and then simplify:

Content:
[MATH: (6x^{2} + x + 1) + (2x^{2} − 3x + 6)|=; 6x^{2} + x + 1 + 2x^{2} − 3x + 6|=; 6x^{2} + 2x^{2}_(⏟)_(x^{2}terms) + x − 3x^(⏞)^(xterms) + 1 + 6_(⏟)_(constants)|=; (6 + 2)x^{2} + (1 − 3)x + 7|=; 8x^{2} − 2x + 7]

sections.normalized_html: Add the polynomials [MATH: x^3-x^2 - 2] and [MATH: -2x^3 + 3x^2-x.]

We put a plus sign between the two polynomials, collect like terms, and then simplify:

[MATH: (x^{3} − x^{2} − 2) + (− 2x^{3} + 3x^{2} − x)|=; x^{3} − x^{2} − 2 − 2x^{3} + 3x^{2} − x|=; x^{3} − 2x^{3} − x^{2} + 3x^{2} − x − 2|=; (1 − 2)x^{3} + (− 1 + 3)x^{2} − x − 2|=; (− 1)x^{3} + (2)x^{2} − x − 2|=; − x^{3} + 2x^{2} − x − 2]

items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that we want to subtract the polynomial [MATH: 2x^2 + x] from the polynomial [MATH: 6x^2 - 3x +1.] To do that, we start by putting a minus sign between the two:

Content:
[MATH: ( 6x^2 - 3x +1) - ( 2x^2 + x )]

Content:
Here, we need to remember to distribute the minus sign. Once we've done that, we can collect like terms and then simplify as usual:

Content:
[MATH: (6x^{2} − 3x + 1) − (2x^{2} + x)|=; 6x^{2} − 3x + 1 − 2x^{2} − x|=; 6x^{2} − 2x^{2} − 3x − x + 1|=; (6 − 2)x^{2} + (− 3 − 1)x + 1|=; 4x^{2} − 4x + 1]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that we have the two polynomials [MATH: 6x^2 + x +1] and [MATH: 2x^2 - 3x + 6], and we want to add them. To do that, we put a plus sign between the two, collect like terms, and then simplify:

[MATH: (6x^{2} + x + 1) + (2x^{2} − 3x + 6)|=; 6x^{2} + x + 1 + 2x^{2} − 3x + 6|=; 6x^{2} + 2x^{2}_(⏟)_(x^{2}terms) + x − 3x^(⏞)^(xterms) + 1 + 6_(⏟)_(constants)|=; (6 + 2)x^{2} + (1 − 3)x + 7|=; 8x^{2} − 2x + 7]
